text:
Ben Kindel is 19 and in his second NHL season with the Penguins, which is already unusual for the 11th pick of the 2025 draft. He has 10 points in 19 games, a 0.53 pace that sits above the 0.37 median for forwards picked around him in their first full season.

The frustrating part is what's happening around him. Pittsburgh has scored 11.9 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, one of the biggest gaps in the league, and that has cost him points. His own finishing is a little light too: four goals on 5.4 expected.

That usually swings back. He's playing 18 minutes a night, carrying the puck into the zone on 56% of his entries last season by Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, and his shot grades out at the 80th percentile by NHL Edge.

The Penguins have won two of his last ten games. What to watch: if the bounces even out, the production should follow, and a 19-year-old with this role can grow into much more.
